transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m getting worried about mistakes I’m making at work. I’m a camera operator and editor, and lately I keep making these technical errors that I really should know better than to make—like labeling camera cards wrong, missing a timecode note, or exporting a client cut with the wrong lower-third, even after I thought I checked it. It’s starting to scare me a bit because these are basic things for my job.
How has your sleep been lately—are you having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or feeling rested when you wake up?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been tracking it closely. I don’t think there’s anything major with my sleep that I’ve noticed, but I can pay more attention to it if that would help.
Have you always had a tendency to make these kinds of careless mistakes, even back in school or earlier jobs, or is this a new pattern that's started more recently?

I think I’ve probably made little mistakes before, but what feels different now is how obvious and avoidable they are. Like, I know how to do this work, and still I’ll label a camera card wrong, miss a timecode note, or export a client cut with the wrong lower-third even after I thought I checked it. That’s the part that scared me enough to come in.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling down, low, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?
I haven’t really noticed that, no. I mean, I’m stressed about the work mistakes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down or losing interest in things lately.
Do you often feel excessively sleepy or find yourself struggling to stay awake during the day, even after what you think was a full night's sleep?
Not that I’ve noticed. I mean, I get tired like anyone, but I’m not usually fighting to stay awake during the day or nodding off after a normal night’s sleep.
Besides these work mistakes, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other areas of your life—like health, finances, or relationships—in a way that feels hard to control?

Not really, no. I mean, I worry about normal things sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m stuck worrying about my health or money or relationships in a way I can’t control. The main thing on my mind has been the mistakes at work.
Thinking back to when you were a child or teenager in school, did you have similar problems with attention, staying focused, or being easily distracted?

Yes, definitely. Even back in elementary school, I remember teachers moving my desk because I was constantly out of my seat or blurting out answers. I’d also end up bothering classmates before I even realized I was doing it.
